subject: EdgeWave Dedicated: burst credits, memory tilt, and pool architecture options
messages:
From: Carlos Hernandez <carlos.hernandez@edgewave.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgewave.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated — questions on burst credits & GPU memory mix

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at EdgeWave liked the latency profiles and the routing/fallback story. A couple of procurement/engineering questions came up while we put together the internal ask:

1) Workload mix: we expect ~65% of tokens to be short-turn interactive chat (95th p50 latency needs), and ~35% to be longer batched inference for embeddings/large queries (32k context).
2) Our engineers lean toward H100 for 32k context models but the cost delta vs A100/L40S is material.
3) We are trying to understand pricing mechanics you mentioned on the call: dedicated reserved commits + a burst credit pool to absorb seasonality. Can you share an example of how commits vs burst credits map to perf/$ for H100 vs A100 vs L40S? Specifically: memory tradeoffs (80GB vs 40GB), and how you price an L40S-heavy mixed pool vs an H100-only pool.

Operational constraints:
- We need a predictable monthly bill for budgeting (finance asks for a committed line item).
- We also want a cushion for marketing spikes: a burst mechanism that won’t require procurement cycles.

Can you send a short term-sheet or example structure your team would propose here? Also flag any required lead times for provisioning H100s.

Thanks,
Carlos
Carlos Hernandez
Head of Infrastructure
EdgeWave

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — questions on burst credits & GPU memory mix

Carlos — thanks, glad the demo landed well. I copied Ben (pricing) and Dylan (solutions) to help with sizing. High-level answers up front, then an example term-sheet attached.

Quick framing: there are three common approaches we recommend depending on how you prioritize latency predictability vs unit cost:

- H100-centric reserved pool: best for consistent high-context workloads (32k). Highest perf/$ for 32k decoding but higher absolute $/GPU-hour. Good when 60–80% of workload requires large context.
- Mixed-pool (H100 + L40S): put L40S behind a routing policy for embeddings and short-turn chat where memory/perf can be traded for cost; route long-contexts to a smaller H100 sub-pool. This often gives the best blended perf/$ when you have mixed traffic.
- A100-80 (or A100-40) balanced pool: single-sku simplicity — cheaper than H100 but worse for 32k latency and memory headroom; useful when you want simpler operational footprint and tighter discounts on larger commits.

Burst credit model example (attached term sheet has numbers):
- Commit: monthly reserved capacity measured in GPU-hours; committed price = base discounted rate.
- Burst credits: not time-limited tokens, but an overdraft window tied to a monthly quota we refill each billing period. Overages consumed beyond burst credits are billed at on-demand uplift.
- Convertibility: unused commit capacity can be converted to burst credits up to a negotiated cap at the end of each quarter (useful for seasonal customers).

Memory/perf examples we can run quickly (ballpark):
- H100-80: best for 32k; expected perf/$ for large-context generation is ~20–30% better than A100-80 on our runtime for your models.
- L40S: excellent for dense embeddings and short-turn chat at a much lower cost per GPU-hour; memory is smaller but throughput for batch embeddings is strong.

Next steps: Ben and Dylan, can you run a quick sizing calc for EdgeWave (65/35 chat/batch split, expected 1.2 billion tokens/mo) and produce a 12-month commit structure with: (a) H100-only option; (b) Mixed H100+L40S with routing; (c) A100-80 single-sku option — include committed and burst credit pricing and an example monthly bill.

Carlos — I attached a draft term sheet (EdgeWave_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf) and a small pool-sizing workbook (EW_pool_sizing_v1.xlsx). Can you confirm a 10–12 week preferred lead time for H100 provisioning or do you need faster?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Redwood Dedicated — questions on burst credits & GPU memory mix

Internal notes / ask — copying Marissa for deal guidance.

Context: EdgeWave is evaluating committed capacity with a desire for a predictable budget line plus a burst cushion. They prefer H100 for large-context models but are price sensitive. Use the attached workbook and the assumptions below. Deliverable: 12-month commit term-sheet for the three options and an illustrative first-month invoice.

Assumptions for sizing (from Carlos): 1.2B tokens/mo, 65% chat (short, latency sensitive), 35% batch/large-context. Peak burst factor = 1.8x baseline during marketing events (approx 3–5 days per month). Region = us-west.

Suggested concession bands to propose:
- 12-month commit (baseline): H100 list price * commit discount 18–20% for >5M GPU-hours/year equivalent; A100 - 25% at same scale; L40S - 30%
- Mixed-pool blended concession: give an extra 4–6% blended discount in exchange for a minimum H100 floor (e.g., at least 20% of committed GPU-hours must be H100).
- Burst credit pricing: include 10% of monthly commit as complimentary burst credits for first 3 months, then 50% of that replenished monthly unless they convert unused commit on the quarter. Extra burst use billed at on-demand uplift (nominal +35% over commit unit price).

Risk/ops notes:
- H100 lead time: estimate 8–12 weeks for dedicated physical pools unless we can reallocate from a nearby capacity region. Late provisioning risk — add a fallback in the contract to temporarily route long-context to A100-80 with guaranteed latency SLA stepdown.
- Observability: include per-route token-level billing and per-GPU utilization reports monthly as part of the package (no extra charge).

Ben/Dylan — please push numbers into the workbook and draft a short term-sheet. Marissa — when you have a moment, advise on whether to hold firm on the 20% H100 floor for mixed-pool asks.

Thanks,
Soojin
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood Dedicated — questions on burst credits & GPU memory mix

Carlos — appreciate the quick turnaround while you were internalizing the demo. Attached is a short, actionable term-sheet that maps to the three options we discussed and an illustrative first-month invoice. Highlights:

Option A — H100-centric (12m commit)
- Minimum commit: 120 H100-equivalent GPU-hours/day (monthly commit = ~36,000 GPU-hours)
- Commit discount: 19% off list for H100 at this scale
- Complimentary burst credits: 10% of monthly commit for first 3 months
- Overages: billed at commit price + 35% uplift
- Lead time: 8–12 weeks

Option B — Mixed pool (H100 + L40S routing) — recommended for your mix
- Commit: blended 70/30 GPU-hour split (H100/L40S) with money-back floor of 20% H100 required
- Blended discount: 24% off blended list if they commit to the H100 floor
- Complimentary burst credits: 10% first 3 months + option to convert unused commit into additional burst credits at quarter end (up to 25% of unused commit)
- Overages: L40S overage billed at blended on-demand uplift (nominal +30%)
- Lead time: L40S immediate; H100 8–12 weeks for dedicated nodes

Option C — A100-80 single-sku (simplicity)
- Commit discount: 26% at the targeted scale
- Lower unit price but expect 15–25% worse latency for 32k context vs H100 on our runtime

Operational add-ons we’ve included at no extra charge for the first 12 months: per-route telemetry, cost-per-token dashboards, and monthly utilization syncs.

Next steps: if you’re comfortable with the mixed-pool option we’ll: (1) lock the blended pricing in a short MOU, (2) schedule a tech sync to finalize routing policies, and (3) start a 12-week provisioning plan for the H100 tranche. I attached the term-sheet (EdgeWave_Dedicated_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf) and the pool sizing workbook (EW_pool_sizing_v1.xlsx) with the modeled numbers used above.

Can you confirm procurement timeline and whether you want us to hold H100 capacity while the MOU is drafted?

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
